analysis.title: Global Economics Daily Points, November 3, 2026
key_insights: Mixed signals on the Iran war are driving volatility in oil, bonds and stocks on US midterm election day. Oil is up about 2% today after yesterday's plunge, pushing bond yields higher, particularly in Canada and Europe.
US stocks are modestly lower (S&P 500 -0.5%, Nasdaq -1.1%) on oil, Apple's results (slowing sales growth, disappointing China), and midterm nervousness.

Scotiabank's Holt argues markets over-trusted Trump's about-face on attacking Iran on Monday, which lowered oil on his own headlines. He sees it as an effort to cut energy prices on election day while Trump keeps warning he could escalate after the vote.

Overnight US attacks on Qeshm Island and more ships struck by mines in the Strait of Hormuz support the escalation narrative. Qatar says negotiations are ongoing, but Holt notes earlier rounds produced nothing because the divisions are too great.
Holt says possible domestic gridlock after the midterms raises foreign policy risks.

Midterm results arrive in staggered fashion from 6pm ET, with 8pm ET the biggest single poll-closing period followed by 9pm ET, and California closing at 11pm ET. Early counts may mislead (a 'red mirage') and markets are likely to be volatile as counting shifts to Democratic areas.

Unless the result is a real blow-out, full results including contested races could take days or weeks. It is unclear whether Trump will accept the results. Most pundits and pollsters expect a Democratic House and possibly a Democratic sweep.

BoC Governor Macklem and Senior Deputy Governor Rogers testify to lawmakers at 11am ET. Holt expects little new and expects Macklem to fade the softer-than-expected monthly GDP and the oil drop, given mixed signals on the Iran war.

The RBA raised the cash rate 25bps to 4.85% in a 6-3 vote, as widely expected. The A$ softened and the Australian curve rallied because the statement dropped the reference to further hikes 'if needed'.
Markets price the RBA as essentially done after 125bps of hikes, with a peak one-in-four chance of another hike in 2027Q1 after a December hold.
US data risk is modest: JOLTS and factory orders at 10am ET, and vehicle sales later in the day.
earnings_insights: Apple reported results that beat expectations (the note says markets were 'unimpressed by Apple's beats'), but sales growth is slowing and China results disappointed. No figures given in the note.

macro_indicators.interpretation: An expected jump from the prior month's 0.1%. Released at 10:00 ET Nov 3.
Modest data risk while markets focus on the midterms.
Raised 25bps in a 6-3 vote. The statement dropped 'increased the cash rate target further if needed', read as signalling the hiking cycle may be over.
Markets price the RBA as basically done after 125bps of hikes, with a hold expected in December.
The BoC hiked last Wednesday. Monthly GDP came in softer than expected.
Yields pushed higher by the 2% rise in oil.

risk_factors: Escalation of the Iran war after the midterms, including mines in the Strait of Hormuz.
Misleading early midterm results ('red mirage') and slow or contested counts.
Domestic political gridlock raising foreign policy risk.
Slowing Apple sales growth and weak China results weighing on tech.
Possible Trump refusal to accept election results.
vol_and_positioning: Markets are described as fragile, with volatility expected from staggered midterm results and 'red mirage' early counts.
Oil plunged on Monday and is up about 2% today, swinging bonds and stocks with it.
geopolitical: US-Iran war: Trump reversed course on attacking Iran on Monday and pointed to talks, while overnight US attacks hit Qeshm Island and more ships were struck by mines in the Strait of Hormuz.
Qatar says negotiations are ongoing, but the note says they have repeatedly failed because the divisions are too great.
Trump has repeatedly warned he could escalate the war again after the US midterm vote.
US midterm elections on November 3, with possible recounts, court challenges and uncertainty over whether Trump will accept the results.

tension_points.bull_case: Trump's Monday reversal on attacking Iran and Qatar's statement that negotiations are ongoing pushed oil sharply lower.
tension_points.bear_case: Holt sees the reversal as an election-day effort to lower energy prices. Qeshm Island attacks, mines striking ships in the Strait of Hormuz and Trump's warnings of escalation after the vote lean the other way.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A US escalation after the midterm vote, or further ship strikes in the Strait of Hormuz.

theme_stances.key_argument: Staggered results and misleading early counts will drive volatility, and contested outcomes could take days or weeks.
theme_stances.evidence: Early results could be misleading, such as the so-called 'red mirage.'

theme_stances.key_argument: Markets over-believed Trump's de-escalation headline, and escalation risk remains after the midterms.
theme_stances.evidence: Most would see through this as an effort to lower energy prices on election day

theme_stances.key_argument: The statement removed the further-hike language, so markets price the RBA as essentially done.
